cl_mdma_vs_mda.q: How is MDA different from MDMA?
cl_mdma_vs_mda.short: It seemed to last longer, with more visuals and less anxiety: still felt at 8 hours, while MDMA had faded by 6. That's one small lab study.
cl_mdma_vs_mda.but: MDA and MDMA weren't tested on the same people. The MDMA group, from earlier studies, was only watched for 6 hours.
how: 12 healthy adults who had used MDA, or MDMA and LSD-type drugs, took MDA and a dummy pill in hospital, not told which. Their results were set beside earlier MDMA results from other people.
MDA brought more visions with eyes closed and more 'spiritual' feelings than MDMA, and less anxiety and loss of control. Both made people feel close to others.
Heart rate rose about 20 beats a minute after MDA and 31 after MDMA, though the paper calls them similar. Top blood pressure rose about 30 points with both.
The paper calls MDA well tolerated but gives no side-effect data at all. Why MDMA is more popular wasn't studied.
cl_mdma_vs_mda.rate: One small lab study of 12 people, set beside MDMA results from different people who were watched for less time. So the differences may come from the people or the timing, not the drugs.

cl_lsd_vs_psilocybin.q: LSD or mushrooms: what's actually different?
cl_lsd_vs_psilocybin.short: Mostly how long it lasts: about 9 to 11 hours for LSD, 6 to 7 for psilocybin, the drug in mushrooms. Otherwise 28 people in a lab rated the trips alike.
cl_lsd_vs_psilocybin.but: Finding no difference in 28 people doesn't prove there is none. And most could tell which drug they'd had.
how: 28 healthy adults each had five hospital days, at least 10 days apart. They got a dummy, two amounts of LSD and two of psilocybin, in random order, not told which.
LSD lasted longer at both amounts. It also began a bit sooner, which the authors put down to it being a liquid, not a capsule.
The higher psilocybin amount raised blood pressure and body temperature a little more. LSD raised heart rate more. Both brought complaints like headaches; nobody had a serious problem.
By the study's own figures, people named the right drug in most sessions, which may have shaped their ratings. It used pure psilocybin in capsules, not mushrooms.
cl_lsd_vs_psilocybin.rate: One careful lab study of 28 people, who took both drugs in random order. But most could tell which drug they had, and 'alike' only means no clear difference was found.

cl_mix_mdma_alcohol.q: What happens when you mix MDMA with alcohol?
cl_mix_mdma_alcohol.short: Just as drunk, but less sleepy, and about as bad on a test at its worst. Blood MDMA also peaked 13% higher, in a lab study of 9 men.
cl_mix_mdma_alcohol.but: Only 9 men, in a lab. Heart measurements were taken but never reported.
how: 9 healthy men who had taken MDMA before each had four lab sessions, a week apart. They got MDMA, alcohol, both, or neither, with dummy pills and drinks so they didn't know which.
With both, the sleepy feeling from alcohol went away. Feeling drunk didn't: if anything, it was rated a bit higher, though not clearly.
On a timed symbol test, scores at their worst fell about as much as with alcohol alone, but for about 1 hour, not 2 to 3. Only with both was reaction time clearly slower than with the dummy.
Blood MDMA peaked 13% higher and blood alcohol 15% lower; the authors call these small changes. Nobody asked the men how well they thought they did, and nobody drove.
cl_mix_mdma_alcohol.rate: One small lab study of 9 young men who knew MDMA well, with one amount of each drug. 'Just as drunk' means no clear difference was found, and the heart results were never reported.

cl_mix_mdma_lsd.q: What if I take LSD and MDMA at the same time?
cl_mix_mdma_lsd.short: Blood pressure and heart rate went higher than on LSD alone, and bad feelings weren't clearly eased. In a lab study of 24 people, top blood pressure was 13 points higher.
cl_mix_mdma_lsd.but: Healthy people took one amount of each, in a calm hospital room. Nothing serious happened, but 24 people can't show rare dangers.
how: 24 healthy adults each had four hospital days, at least 10 days apart. They got LSD, MDMA, both at once, or a dummy, in random order and without being told which.

With both, top blood pressure averaged 150, against 137 on LSD alone and 148 on MDMA alone; heart rate 100 beats a minute, against 92 and 95. Body temperature was not clearly higher than on LSD alone.
Bad-feeling, fear and complaint scores were not clearly lower than on LSD alone. Nobody had a serious problem. On nausea, the paper contradicts itself.
The two drugs changed each other's blood levels: more LSD stayed in the blood for longer, while MDMA peaked lower and later.
cl_mix_mdma_lsd.rate: One careful lab study of 24 healthy people, with one amount of each drug taken together. The blood pressure results are clear; the rest rests on people's own ratings, and rare dangers can't show up in so few.

mdma.statement: In a lab study, MDA brought more visions than MDMA, but less anxiety.
mdma.why: That's what 12 people on MDA reported, set against MDMA results from other people in earlier studies, so it's a weak comparison.

mdma.statement: In a lab study, MDA's effects lasted longer than MDMA's.
mdma.why: Still felt at 8 hours, while MDMA had faded by 6. But MDMA was only watched for 6 hours, in other people.

lsd.statement: In a lab test, LSD and psilocybin trips felt much alike. The big difference was how long they lasted.
lsd.why: In 28 people, LSD lasted about 9 to 11 hours and psilocybin 6 to 7. Ratings barely differed, but that's no proof they're the same.

lsd.statement: Adding MDMA to LSD has been shown to make a bad trip less likely.
lsd.why: In 24 people, bad-feeling and fear scores weren't clearly lower than on LSD alone, and nobody tested it at a party.

psilocybin.statement: Most people can't tell LSD from psilocybin if not told which they got.
psilocybin.why: By the 28-person study's own figures, people named the right drug in most sessions, though the trips were rated alike.

interactions.statement: Taking MDMA with alcohol makes you feel less drunk.
interactions.why: In a lab study of 9 men, MDMA took away alcohol's sleepiness, not the drunk feeling, and test scores still dropped.

interactions.statement: Taking MDMA with LSD pushes heart rate and blood pressure higher than LSD alone.
interactions.why: In a lab study of 24 people, they rose about as high as on MDMA alone. Body temperature wasn't clearly higher.

alcohol.statement: With MDMA, blood alcohol was a bit lower, yet people felt just as drunk.
alcohol.why: 15% lower at its peak, in 9 men, but drunk ratings didn't fall, and test scores at their worst dropped about as much.
